1	# Vision Dataset Workbench
2	
3	Vision Dataset Workbench is a local, CPU-friendly command-line foundation for organizing image datasets. It stores a small manifest beside the dataset, imports image metadata without uploading files, and reports basic dataset statistics.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	- Python 3.11 or newer
8	- No third-party runtime dependencies
9	
10	## Quick start
11	
12	```bash
13	python3 -m vision_workbench init ./workspace
14	python3 -m vision_workbench add ./workspace ./examples/cat.jpg --label cat
15	python3 -m vision_workbench summary ./workspace
16	```
17	
18	The manifest is written to `.vision-workbench/manifest.json`. Importing the same file twice is idempotent because records are keyed by the file content hash. Imports, batch writes, undos and plan creation are serialized by a single workspace lock and committed through the same write-ahead journal, so several local processes can operate on one workspace at once: every successful operation survives, concurrent imports of different content all land, and duplicate imports report `already present` once while keeping the first registration's source and label.
19	
20	A single-file `add` registers the file's full SHA-256 digest, byte size and
21	resolved absolute source path, and all three are read from the same stable
22	regular file: the source is checked before and after the read, and the read
23	itself is pinned to the confirmed file. If the source is rewritten, appended
24	to, truncated, deleted and recreated, or replaced by another file (even one
25	with identical content, size and modification time) while it is being
26	confirmed or read — or if the path vanishes, becomes a directory or a
27	symlink, or cannot be opened or read in full — the import fails with the
28	source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
29	happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
30	path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
31	target imported.
32	
33	## Importing a directory
34	
35	A whole directory of images can be registered in one batch:
36	
37	```bash
38	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --label cat
39	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --recursive
40	```
41	
42	(The shorter `import` alias is equivalent.)
43	
44	- Only regular files with an extension of `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`,
45	  `.gif` or `.webp` (matched case-insensitively) are candidates. Symlinks
46	  and other entry types never qualify; recursion stays on the top level
47	  unless `--recursive` is given and never descends through symlinked
48	  directories. Files that appear after the scan are left for the next
49	  import.
50	- Candidates are ordered by their path relative to the source directory,
51	  with `/` separators, compared by Unicode code point.
52	- Samples are identified by their full SHA-256 digest. When several
53	  candidates share content that the workspace does not yet know, only the
54	  sorted-first candidate is added; the rest report `duplicate`. Digests
55	  already in the workspace always report `duplicate` and keep their
56	  original source, label and revision history — the batch label never
57	  overwrites an existing record.
58	- `--label` applies only to genuinely new samples. Omitting it leaves
59	  them unlabeled; the empty string also means unlabeled; any other string
60	  is kept literally.
61	- The result is JSON: the candidate count, the number added, the number
62	  of duplicates, and every candidate's relative path, full digest and
63	  `added`/`duplicate` status in scan order. Empty directories and
64	  all-duplicate imports succeed with zero added.
65	- The batch is all-or-nothing: a missing or non-directory source, a
66	  directory that cannot be scanned, a candidate that cannot be read in
67	  full, or a candidate whose identity, size or modification time changes
68	  while it is read fails the whole import with the path and reason and
69	  leaves no new samples. With `--recursive`, a subdirectory that was
70	  confirmed as a real directory and is then replaced by a symbolic link —
71	  wherever the link points — likewise fails the whole import with the
72	  subdirectory's path, rather than following the link or skipping the
73	  directory; the link target's images are neither imported nor reported
74	  as duplicates, and directories that were symlinks from the start are
75	  still simply ignored. The batch commits through the same journal as
76	  single-file imports, so an interruption shows either the old state or
77	  the complete batch, and concurrent label batches are never lost.
78	
79	## Split plans
80	
81	A split plan divides every sample currently in the manifest into a
82	train/validation/test set. Plans are saved under
83	`.vision-workbench/splits/<name>.json` and never change afterwards.
84	
85	```bash
86	python3 -m vision_workbench split create ./workspace baseline \
87	    --seed 42 --train 0.6 --validation 0.2 --test 0.2
88	python3 -m vision_workbench split show ./workspace baseline
89	```
90	
91	- The three ratios must be finite numbers in `[0, 1]` that sum to exactly
92	  one; any of them may be zero. Decimals (`0.1`) and fractions (`1/3`) are
93	  both accepted and handled with exact rational arithmetic.
94	- Stratification guarantees that, for every class and for the dataset as a
95	  whole, each set's count differs from its proportional expectation by
96	  strictly less than one — even for classes with one or two samples.
97	- Assignments depend only on sample content digests, labels and the seed,
98	  so they are stable across import order, manifest ordering, workspace
99	  location and restarts. Samples are listed by digest in each set.
100	- Unlabeled samples (no label or an empty label) form their own stratum,
101	  reported under the empty-string key `""`; a real class literally named
102	  `unlabeled` is kept separate.
103	- Creating under an existing name reuses the plan only when the seed,
104	  ratios, sample identities and labels all match; otherwise it reports a
105	  name conflict and leaves the original untouched. Sample identities and
106	  labels are snapshotted from one complete manifest state, so a batch that
107	  changes several labels is seen wholly before or wholly after the plan,
108	  never half-applied. Concurrent creation of one name is atomic: exactly
109	  one request creates it, identical requests reuse it and differing
110	  requests conflict; plans with different names all save, and a plan is
111	  only ever read whole or reported as not found.
112	
113	## Exporting a split plan
114	
115	A saved split plan can be exported as a portable, offline ZIP package:
116	
117	```bash
118	python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip
119	```
120	
121	- The package contains `train/`, `validation/` and `test/` directories,
122	  each with the same numbered ImageFolder class directories (`class_01`,
123	  `class_02`, ...), plus a UTF-8 `manifest.json`. Samples are stored as
124	  `<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>`.
125	- The export uses only the saved plan: its samples, labels, set
126	  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
127	  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
128	  writes to the workspace.
129	- All sets share one class directory numbering, even when a class has no
130	  samples in a set. Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and
131	  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
132	  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
133	  paths are written.
134	- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
135	- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
136	  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
137	  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
138	  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
139	  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
140	- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
141	  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
142	  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
143	- A single sample at or above 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes of uncompressed
144	  content) is written as a ZIP64 entry automatically; large and ordinary
145	  samples may coexist in one plan and one package, and the large entry is
146	  still streamed in fixed chunks, so exporting it never needs memory for
147	  the whole file. This also covers multi-gigabyte content that compresses
148	  well: the decision follows the uncompressed size, so a tiny resulting
149	  package is not rejected. Plans containing only smaller samples keep
150	  exactly the classic archive format, byte for byte — ZIP64 fields appear
151	  only in the entries that require them. The manifest, the result counts
152	  and the set/class layout are identical either way, and packages remain
153	  extractable with standard ZIP64-aware tools.
154	- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
155	  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
156	  ```bash
157	  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
158	      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
159	  ```
160	  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
161	  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
162	  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
163	  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
164	  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
165	  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
166	  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
167	  point is used. The selected copy is pinned to the actual read: the path
168	  is lstat()ed without following symlinks, opened without following a
169	  final symlink, and the opened descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be
170	  the exact regular file (same device and inode) captured during the
171	  lookup — the check covers the object that is really read, not just one
172	  look at the path before it opens. If the selected path is replaced
173	  after the lookup but before or while it is opened by another regular
174	  file — even one with identical content, size and modification time —
175	  or by a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, the whole
176	  export fails with the sample digest, the selected source path and the
177	  reason; no other same-content copy is substituted and the plan's
178	  recorded source path is not used as a fallback.
179	
180	  The directory walk is itself pinned to directory descriptors rather
181	  than path strings: each directory is entered with `openat`
182	  (`O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_DIRECTORY`) relative to its parent's descriptor
183	  and verified with `fstatat`, and the confirmed root stays open for the
184	  whole export. A subdirectory that is a real directory when the walk
185	  first reaches it but is replaced by a symlink before it is entered,
186	  while its contents are read, after the lookup or while the package is
187	  copied fails the whole export with the changed directory's path and
188	  the symlink reason — whether the link points outside the specified
189	  directory, inside it, or at the directory moved to its new location,
190	  and at any nesting level. The link's target is never read, matched or
191	  packaged, even if it holds a file byte-identical to the planned
192	  sample; no other normal copy and no still-readable recorded source are
193	  substituted. Before each matched file is copied its ancestor
194	  directories are re-verified the same way, and after all samples are
195	  streamed every directory from the walk is verified once more before
196	  the ZIP is published, so the target ZIP is never created and no
197	  incomplete export file remains. Only entries that are already
198	  symlinks the first time the walk meets them are skipped, as before.
199	
200	  Files unrelated to the
201	  plan are read (an unreadable file anywhere fails the export) but never
202	  included. The plan still decides
203	  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
204	  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
205	  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
206	  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
207	  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
208	  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
209	  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
210	- The target name is owned only once the whole package has been generated
211	  and fsynced and the source verification has passed, so a reader never
212	  sees a half-written file.  The name must be free both when the export
213	  starts and at the moment the finished package is published: another
214	  program that creates a file at the target path while the images are
215	  copied or compressed — even an empty file or one byte-identical to the
216	  package, and even in the last instant before publication — makes the
217	  export fail with the user-given target path as a name-already-taken
218	  conflict, a non-zero exit status and no result on standard output.
219	  That occupant is never overwritten, unlinked or moved, its content and
220	  file type are preserved, and this run's temporary package is removed.
221	  A symbolic link at the name counts as occupied too, including one that
222	  points at a location that does not exist; whether the link is there at
223	  the start or appears during the export, the link itself and its target
224	  are left in place and the ZIP is never written through it.  There is no
225	  overwrite option and no automatic alternative file name.  A failure or
226	  interruption otherwise leaves no incomplete file, and concurrent
227	  exports to the same path are serialized so at most one succeeds and the
228	  rest fail clearly with the same conflict.
229	- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
230	  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
231	  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
232	  do not matter.
233	
234	## Finding samples by label
235	
236	Samples can be listed by their current category label, so a class leads
237	straight to the full sample summaries needed for the label queries and
238	batch updates below — no need to page through the dataset listing.
239	
240	```bash
241	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace cat     # a normal class
242	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace 猫      # Chinese text, kept as-is
243	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace ''      # unlabeled samples
244	python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace unlabeled  # the literal class
245	```
246	
247	The result is readable UTF-8 JSON: the queried label, the match count and
248	the sample list, each record giving the full SHA-256 digest, the source
249	path saved at first registration, the byte size and the current label.
250	Records are sorted ascending by full digest and `count` always equals the
251	list length. A digest is listed once no matter how many paths once
252	imported identical content, with the source from its first registration.
253	
254	- Matching is exact on the **current** registered label: case, leading or
255	  trailing whitespace and path separators are matched literally and are
256	  never trimmed, rewritten or interpreted as paths. Querying `cat` does
257	  not return `Cat` or `cat ` (cat followed by a space).
258	- The empty string queries **unlabeled** samples: records whose label is
259	  `null` or `""` both match, and every returned record shows its label as
260	  `null`. Querying the text `unlabeled` instead returns only samples
261	  whose real class is literally named `unlabeled`; it never includes
262	  unlabeled samples and does not use the summary statistics' display that
263	  merges the two.

# Vision Dataset Workbench

Vision Dataset Workbench is a local, CPU-friendly command-line foundation for organizing image datasets. It stores a small manifest beside the dataset, imports image metadata without uploading files, and reports basic dataset statistics.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- No third-party runtime dependencies

## Quick start

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench init ./workspace
python3 -m vision_workbench add ./workspace ./examples/cat.jpg --label cat
python3 -m vision_workbench summary ./workspace
```

The manifest is written to `.vision-workbench/manifest.json`. Importing the same file twice is idempotent because records are keyed by the file content hash. Imports, batch writes, undos and plan creation are serialized by a single workspace lock and committed through the same write-ahead journal, so several local processes can operate on one workspace at once: every successful operation survives, concurrent imports of different content all land, and duplicate imports report `already present` once while keeping the first registration's source and label.

A single-file `add` registers the file's full SHA-256 digest, byte size and
resolved absolute source path, and all three are read from the same stable
regular file: the source is checked before and after the read, and the read
itself is pinned to the confirmed file. If the source is rewritten, appended
to, truncated, deleted and recreated, or replaced by another file (even one
with identical content, size and modification time) while it is being
confirmed or read — or if the path vanishes, becomes a directory or a
symlink, or cannot be opened or read in full — the import fails with the
source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
target imported.

## Importing a directory

A whole directory of images can be registered in one batch:

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --label cat
python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --recursive
```

(The shorter `import` alias is equivalent.)

- Only regular files with an extension of `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`,
  `.gif` or `.webp` (matched case-insensitively) are candidates. Symlinks
  and other entry types never qualify; recursion stays on the top level
  unless `--recursive` is given and never descends through symlinked
  directories. Files that appear after the scan are left for the next
  import.
- Candidates are ordered by their path relative to the source directory,
  with `/` separators, compared by Unicode code point.
- Samples are identified by their full SHA-256 digest. When several
  candidates share content that the workspace does not yet know, only the
  sorted-first candidate is added; the rest report `duplicate`. Digests
  already in the workspace always report `duplicate` and keep their
  original source, label and revision history — the batch label never
  overwrites an existing record.
- `--label` applies only to genuinely new samples. Omitting it leaves
  them unlabeled; the empty string also means unlabeled; any other string
  is kept literally.
- The result is JSON: the candidate count, the number added, the number
  of duplicates, and every candidate's relative path, full digest and
  `added`/`duplicate` status in scan order. Empty directories and
  all-duplicate imports succeed with zero added.
- The batch is all-or-nothing: a missing or non-directory source, a
  directory that cannot be scanned, a candidate that cannot be read in
  full, or a candidate whose identity, size or modification time changes
  while it is read fails the whole import with the path and reason and
  leaves no new samples. With `--recursive`, a subdirectory that was
  confirmed as a real directory and is then replaced by a symbolic link —
  wherever the link points — likewise fails the whole import with the
  subdirectory's path, rather than following the link or skipping the
  directory; the link target's images are neither imported nor reported
  as duplicates, and directories that were symlinks from the start are
  still simply ignored. The batch commits through the same journal as
  single-file imports, so an interruption shows either the old state or
  the complete batch, and concurrent label batches are never lost.

## Split plans

A split plan divides every sample currently in the manifest into a
train/validation/test set. Plans are saved under
`.vision-workbench/splits/<name>.json` and never change afterwards.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench split create ./workspace baseline \
    --seed 42 --train 0.6 --validation 0.2 --test 0.2
python3 -m vision_workbench split show ./workspace baseline
```

- The three ratios must be finite numbers in `[0, 1]` that sum to exactly
  one; any of them may be zero. Decimals (`0.1`) and fractions (`1/3`) are
  both accepted and handled with exact rational arithmetic.
- Stratification guarantees that, for every class and for the dataset as a
  whole, each set's count differs from its proportional expectation by
  strictly less than one — even for classes with one or two samples.
- Assignments depend only on sample content digests, labels and the seed,
  so they are stable across import order, manifest ordering, workspace
  location and restarts. Samples are listed by digest in each set.
- Unlabeled samples (no label or an empty label) form their own stratum,
  reported under the empty-string key `""`; a real class literally named
  `unlabeled` is kept separate.
- Creating under an existing name reuses the plan only when the seed,
  ratios, sample identities and labels all match; otherwise it reports a
  name conflict and leaves the original untouched. Sample identities and
  labels are snapshotted from one complete manifest state, so a batch that
  changes several labels is seen wholly before or wholly after the plan,
  never half-applied. Concurrent creation of one name is atomic: exactly
  one request creates it, identical requests reuse it and differing
  requests conflict; plans with different names all save, and a plan is
  only ever read whole or reported as not found.

## Exporting a split plan

A saved split plan can be exported as a portable, offline ZIP package:

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip
```

- The package contains `train/`, `validation/` and `test/` directories,
  each with the same numbered ImageFolder class directories (`class_01`,
  `class_02`, ...), plus a UTF-8 `manifest.json`. Samples are stored as
  `<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>`.
- The export uses only the saved plan: its samples, labels, set
  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
  writes to the workspace.
- All sets share one class directory numbering, even when a class has no
  samples in a set. Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and
  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
  paths are written.
- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
- A single sample at or above 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes of uncompressed
  content) is written as a ZIP64 entry automatically; large and ordinary
  samples may coexist in one plan and one package, and the large entry is
  still streamed in fixed chunks, so exporting it never needs memory for
  the whole file. This also covers multi-gigabyte content that compresses
  well: the decision follows the uncompressed size, so a tiny resulting
  package is not rejected. Plans containing only smaller samples keep
  exactly the classic archive format, byte for byte — ZIP64 fields appear
  only in the entries that require them. The manifest, the result counts
  and the set/class layout are identical either way, and packages remain
  extractable with standard ZIP64-aware tools.
- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
  ```bash
  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
  ```
  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
  point is used. The selected copy is pinned to the actual read: the path
  is lstat()ed without following symlinks, opened without following a
  final symlink, and the opened descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be
  the exact regular file (same device and inode) captured during the
  lookup — the check covers the object that is really read, not just one
  look at the path before it opens. If the selected path is replaced
  after the lookup but before or while it is opened by another regular
  file — even one with identical content, size and modification time —
  or by a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, the whole
  export fails with the sample digest, the selected source path and the
  reason; no other same-content copy is substituted and the plan's
  recorded source path is not used as a fallback.

  The directory walk is itself pinned to directory descriptors rather
  than path strings: each directory is entered with `openat`
  (`O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_DIRECTORY`) relative to its parent's descriptor
  and verified with `fstatat`, and the confirmed root stays open for the
  whole export. A subdirectory that is a real directory when the walk
  first reaches it but is replaced by a symlink before it is entered,
  while its contents are read, after the lookup or while the package is
  copied fails the whole export with the changed directory's path and
  the symlink reason — whether the link points outside the specified
  directory, inside it, or at the directory moved to its new location,
  and at any nesting level. The link's target is never read, matched or
  packaged, even if it holds a file byte-identical to the planned
  sample; no other normal copy and no still-readable recorded source are
  substituted. Before each matched file is copied its ancestor
  directories are re-verified the same way, and after all samples are
  streamed every directory from the walk is verified once more before
  the ZIP is published, so the target ZIP is never created and no
  incomplete export file remains. Only entries that are already
  symlinks the first time the walk meets them are skipped, as before.

  Files unrelated to the
  plan are read (an unreadable file anywhere fails the export) but never
  included. The plan still decides
  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
- The target name is owned only once the whole package has been generated
  and fsynced and the source verification has passed, so a reader never
  sees a half-written file.  The name must be free both when the export
  starts and at the moment the finished package is published: another
  program that creates a file at the target path while the images are
  copied or compressed — even an empty file or one byte-identical to the
  package, and even in the last instant before publication — makes the
  export fail with the user-given target path as a name-already-taken
  conflict, a non-zero exit status and no result on standard output.
  That occupant is never overwritten, unlinked or moved, its content and
  file type are preserved, and this run's temporary package is removed.
  A symbolic link at the name counts as occupied too, including one that
  points at a location that does not exist; whether the link is there at
  the start or appears during the export, the link itself and its target
  are left in place and the ZIP is never written through it.  There is no
  overwrite option and no automatic alternative file name.  A failure or
  interruption otherwise leaves no incomplete file, and concurrent
  exports to the same path are serialized so at most one succeeds and the
  rest fail clearly with the same conflict.
- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
  do not matter.

## Finding samples by label

Samples can be listed by their current category label, so a class leads
straight to the full sample summaries needed for the label queries and
batch updates below — no need to page through the dataset listing.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace cat     # a normal class
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace 猫      # Chinese text, kept as-is
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace ''      # unlabeled samples
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace unlabeled  # the literal class
```

The result is readable UTF-8 JSON: the queried label, the match count and
the sample list, each record giving the full SHA-256 digest, the source
path saved at first registration, the byte size and the current label.
Records are sorted ascending by full digest and `count` always equals the
list length. A digest is listed once no matter how many paths once
imported identical content, with the source from its first registration.

- Matching is exact on the **current** registered label: case, leading or
  trailing whitespace and path separators are matched literally and are
  never trimmed, rewritten or interpreted as paths. Querying `cat` does
  not return `Cat` or `cat ` (cat followed by a space).
- The empty string queries **unlabeled** samples: records whose label is
  `null` or `""` both match, and every returned record shows its label as
  `null`. Querying the text `unlabeled` instead returns only samples
  whose real class is literally named `unlabeled`; it never includes
  unlabeled samples and does not use the summary statistics' display that
  merges the two.
- An empty workspace or a label with no matches is a normal result with
  `count` 0 and an empty list, not an error.
- The query reads only registered records. A successful batch update or
  undo is reflected by the next query; labels snapshotted in saved split
  plans neither match nor are changed, and a source image that has since
  moved, been deleted or become unreadable is still returned — the source
  file is never reopened and its recorded path is never updated.

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

## Batch label updates

Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
UTF-8 JSON file:

```json
{
  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
  "changes": [
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
  ]
}
```

- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
  named `unlabeled`).
- The whole batch is verified before anything is written: an unknown
  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
  number and writes no history.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
python3 -m vision_workbench find-label ./workspace <label>  # samples of one label
python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
```

See [Finding samples by label](#finding-samples-by-label) for the
`find-label` query, including the empty-string query for unlabeled
samples.

Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
conflict.

`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
changed. Failed batches never enter history.

`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
`already-undone`.

Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
apply.

137	        self.lock_path = self.state_directory / LOCK_NAME
138	        self.transaction_path = self.state_directory / TRANSACTION_NAME
139	        # A crash mid-commit can leave a prepared transaction; finish it
140	        # before any operation observes the workspace.
141	        self._recover_if_needed()

143	    def initialize(self) -> None:
144	        # The empty-manifest decision is made under the workspace lock so a
145	        # concurrent first import cannot have its sample replaced by an empty
146	        # dataset created from a stale "manifest missing" observation.
147	        with self._locked(create=True):
148	            if not self.manifest_path.exists():
149	                self._write_json_atomic(
150	                    self.manifest_path, {"schema_version": 1, "items": []}
151	                )

153	    def add(self, source: Path, label: str | None = None) -> ImportResult:
154	        self.initialize()
155	        file_path = source.resolve(strict=True)
156	        if not file_path.is_file():
157	            raise ValueError(f"Not a regular file: {source}")
158	        # Hashing is pure I/O on the source file; do it before taking the
159	        # workspace lock so concurrent imports of different files hash in
160	        # parallel and only serialize for the manifest check-and-commit.
161	        # The digest and the size must describe one stable file: the read
162	        # fails if the file's identity, size or modification time changes
163	        # around or during the read, so a source being rewritten or
164	        # replaced is rejected instead of registering a digest/size pair
165	        # that never coexisted.
166	        digest, size = self._read_stable(file_path, str(file_path))
167	        with self._locked(create=True):
168	            manifest = self._read()
169	            if any(item["sha256"] == digest for item in manifest["items"]):
170	                # Re-import never overwrites the registered source, label or
171	                # revision: the first report of a digest owns its metadata.
172	                return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=False)
173	            manifest["items"].append(
174	                {
175	                    "sha256": digest,
176	                    "source": str(file_path),
177	                    "size": size,
178	                    "label": label,
179	                }
180	            )
181	            manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
182	            # Commit through the same journal as batches so the import is
183	            # crash-safe and cannot clobber a batch committed concurrently.
184	            self._commit(manifest, self._read_history())
185	            return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=True)

187	    def import_directory(
188	        self, source: Path, label: str | None = None, recursive: bool = False
189	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
190	        """Import every accepted image file under a source directory at once.
191	
192	        Candidates are regular files (never symlinks or other entry types)
193	        whose lower-cased extension is one of :data:`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`;
194	        recursion stays on the top level unless ``recursive`` is set and
195	        never descends through symlinked directories.  They are ordered by
196	        path relative to the source directory, with ``/`` separators,
197	        compared by Unicode code point.
198	
199	        Every candidate is read in full and identified by its full
200	        SHA-256 digest.  A digest already in the workspace, or first seen
201	        on an earlier candidate in this same import, is reported as a
202	        duplicate: the earliest sorted candidate owns the registration and
203	        later paths never overwrite its source or label.  The supplied
204	        label is attached only to genuinely new samples; ``None`` and the
205	        empty string both mean unlabeled.
206	
207	        The whole batch commits as one journal transaction.  The import
208	        fails entirely (no new samples) when the source is missing or not
209	        a directory, a directory that should be visited cannot be scanned,
210	        a candidate cannot be read in full, a candidate's identity,
211	        size or modification time changes while it is being read, or a
212	        subdirectory confirmed as a real directory is replaced by a
213	        symbolic link before its scan or before its candidates finish
214	        reading — the link target's images are never imported or even
215	        reported as duplicates.
216	        """
217	        self.initialize()
218	        source_path = Path(source)
219	        if not source_path.exists():
220	            raise ValueError(f"source directory does not exist: {source}")
221	        if not source_path.is_dir():
222	            raise ValueError(f"source is not a directory: {source}")
223	        root = source_path.resolve()
224	
225	        rel_paths, confirmed_dirs = self._scan_image_files(root, recursive)
226	        # Read (and re-stat) every candidate before taking the workspace
227	        # lock: I/O overlaps with peers, and a file that changes mid-read
228	        # fails the whole batch before anything is committed.  A confirmed
229	        # subdirectory swapped for a symlink is never read through: every
230	        # candidate's ancestor directories are re-checked before it is
231	        # opened, the open itself is pinned to the confirmed ancestor
232	        # directories with O_NOFOLLOW descriptors, and the confirmed
233	        # directories are checked once more after all reads, so the link
234	        # target's images cannot be imported or even reported as
235	        # duplicates.
236	        candidates = []
237	        for rel_path in rel_paths:
238	            ancestor = root
239	            for part in Path(rel_path).parts[:-1]:
240	                ancestor = ancestor / part
241	                self._raise_if_now_symlink(ancestor)
242	            candidates.append(self._read_candidate(root / rel_path, rel_path))
243	        for directory in confirmed_dirs:
244	            self._raise_if_now_symlink(directory)
245	
246	        with self._locked(create=True):
247	            manifest = self._read()
248	            history = self._read_history()
249	            known = {item["sha256"] for item in manifest["items"]}
250	
251	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
252	            new_items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
253	            for rel_path, abs_path, digest, size in candidates:
254	                if digest in known:
255	                    status = "duplicate"
256	                else:
257	                    status = "added"
258	                    known.add(digest)
259	                    new_items.append(
260	                        {
261	                            "sha256": digest,
262	                            "source": str(abs_path.resolve()),
263	                            "size": size,
264	                            "label": label,
265	                        }
266	                    )
267	                results.append(
268	                    {"path": rel_path, "sha256": digest, "status": status}
269	                )
270	
271	            if new_items:
272	                manifest["items"].extend(new_items)
273	                manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
274	                # One journal commit for the whole batch: an interruption
275	                # leaves either the old state or every new sample together.
276	                self._commit(manifest, history)
277	
278	        added = sum(1 for result in results if result["status"] == "added")
279	        duplicates = len(results) - added
280	        return {
281	            "directory": str(root),
282	            "recursive": recursive,
283	            "label": label,
284	            "candidate_count": len(results),
285	            "added": added,
286	            "duplicates": duplicates,
287	            "candidates": results,
288	        }

290	    def _scan_image_files(
291	        self, root: Path, recursive: bool
292	    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[Path]]:
293	        """Return accepted files and the real directories descended into.
294	
295	        The first element lists accepted files as ``/``-separated paths
296	        relative to root; the second lists every subdirectory confirmed as
297	        a real directory and descended into (empty unless ``recursive``).
298	
299	        Only real regular files qualify; symlinks and other entry types are
300	        skipped, and recursion never follows symlinked directories.  Any
301	        directory that should be visited but cannot be scanned fails the
302	        whole import with the path and reason.  Every confirmed
303	        subdirectory is opened through its pinned parent directory with
304	        ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` and scanned through that descriptor,
305	        so a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic link at any moment before
306	        or during its scan fails the whole import instead of the link
307	        target being scanned.  The confirmed list lets the caller
308	        re-verify the directories once more after the candidate reads.
309	        """
310	        rel_paths: list[str] = []
311	        confirmed_dirs: list[Path] = []
312	
313	        def classify(
314	            directory: Path, fd_or_path: Any
315	        ) -> list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]:
316	            try:
317	                entries = list(os.scandir(fd_or_path))
318	            except OSError as error:
319	                raise ValueError(
320	                    f"cannot scan directory {directory}: {error}"
321	                ) from error
322	            found: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]] = []
323	            for entry in entries:
324	                try:
325	                    is_file = entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
326	                    is_dir = (
327	                        not is_file
328	                        and recursive
329	                        and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
330	                    )
331	                except OSError as error:
332	                    raise ValueError(
333	                        f"cannot inspect entry {directory / entry.name}: {error}"
334	                    ) from error
335	                found.append((entry.name, is_file, is_dir))
336	            return found
337	
338	        def walk(
339	            directory: Path,
340	            rel_prefix: str,
341	            parent_fd: int,
342	            entries: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]],
343	        ) -> None:
344	            for name, is_file, is_dir in entries:
345	                if is_file:
346	                    if Path(name).suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS:
347	                        rel_paths.append(rel_prefix + name)
348	                elif is_dir:
349	                    subdirectory = directory / name
350	                    # Open the confirmed subdirectory through the pinned
351	                    # parent with O_NOFOLLOW and scan the descriptor
352	                    # itself: a symlink swapped onto the path by now fails
353	                    # the whole import here, and the link target is never
354	                    # scanned.
355	                    try:
356	                        child_fd = self._open_real_directory(
357	                            name, parent_fd, subdirectory
358	                        )
359	                    except OSError as error:
360	                        raise ValueError(
361	                            f"cannot scan directory {subdirectory}: {error}"
362	                        ) from error
363	                    try:
364	                        child_entries = classify(subdirectory, child_fd)
365	                        confirmed_dirs.append(subdirectory)
366	                        walk(
367	                            subdirectory,
368	                            rel_prefix + name + "/",
369	                            child_fd,
370	                            child_entries,
371	                        )
372	                    finally:
373	                        os.close(child_fd)
374	
375	        try:
376	            root_fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
377	        except OSError as error:
378	            raise ValueError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
379	        try:
380	            walk(root, "", root_fd, classify(root, root))
381	        finally:
382	            os.close(root_fd)
383	        # Unicode code point order on the slash-separated relative path.
384	        rel_paths.sort()
385	        return rel_paths, confirmed_dirs
386	
387	    @staticmethod
388	    def _open_real_directory(name: str, dir_fd: int | None, path: Path) -> int:
389	        """Open a confirmed directory, refusing a symlink swapped onto it.
390	
391	        The open uses ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` — relative to the
392	        pinned parent descriptor when ``dir_fd`` is given — so a symbolic
393	        link (or any non-directory) that replaced the confirmed directory
394	        is never descended through.  A symlink swap raises the import's
395	        "directory changed" error naming the replaced path; any other
396	        open failure propagates as the underlying :class:`OSError`.
397	        """
398	        try:
399	            return os.open(name, _DIRECTORY_OPEN_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
400	        except OSError as error:
401	            # Linux reports a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY
402	            # as ENOTDIR rather than ELOOP, so confirm via lstat() either
403	            # way.
404	            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
405	                try:
406	                    current = os.lstat(path)
407	                except OSError:
408	                    current = None
409	                if current is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
410	                    raise ValueError(
411	                        f"directory changed during import: {path} "
412	                        "is now a symbolic link"
413	                    ) from error
414	            raise
415	
416	    @staticmethod
417	    def _raise_if_now_symlink(directory: Path) -> None:
418	        """Fail if a previously confirmed real directory is now a symlink.
419	
420	        A path that vanished is left to the candidate reads (or ignored
421	        when the directory held no candidates); only the symlink swap is
422	        rejected here, because following the link would import the target's
423	        images against the no-symlinked-directories rule.
424	        """
425	        try:
426	            current = os.lstat(directory)
427	        except OSError:
428	            return
429	        if stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
430	            raise ValueError(
431	                f"directory changed during import: {directory} "
432	                "is now a symbolic link"
433	            )

435	    def _read_candidate(
436	        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
437	    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
438	        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.
439	
440	        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
441	        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
442	
443	        Every ancestor directory of the candidate is re-opened from the
444	        source root with ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW``, each relative to its
445	        pinned parent, and the candidate itself is opened relative to its
446	        pinned parent directory: a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic
447	        link since the scan fails the whole import here, and the link
448	        target's images are never opened — no matter when the swap lands.
449	        """
450	        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
451	        root = path
452	        for _ in parts:
453	            root = root.parent
454	        try:
455	            fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
456	        except OSError as error:
457	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}") from error
458	        try:
459	            ancestor = root
460	            for part in parts[:-1]:
461	                ancestor = ancestor / part
462	                try:
463	                    next_fd = self._open_real_directory(part, fd, ancestor)
464	                except OSError as error:
465	                    raise ValueError(
466	                        f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}"
467	                    ) from error
468	                os.close(fd)
469	                fd = next_fd
470	            digest, size = self._read_stable(
471	                path, rel_path, dir_fd=fd, name=parts[-1]
472	            )
473	        finally:
474	            os.close(fd)
475	        return rel_path, path, digest, size
476	
477	    @staticmethod
478	    def _read_stable(
479	        path: Path,
480	        display: str,
481	        *,
482	        dir_fd: int | None = None,
483	        name: str | None = None,
484	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
485	        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.
486	
487	        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
488	        regular file: the path is lstat()ed without following symlinks
489	        and opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, the opened descriptor is
490	        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed, and the
491	        path is lstat()ed again after the read, requiring the same
492	        object with the same size and modification time.  Any identity,
493	        size or modification-time change — in-place rewrites, appends,
494	        truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing the path with
495	        another file, even one with identical content, size and mtime —
496	        fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing path, a
497	        non-regular file and any open or read error.
498	
499	        The confirm/open/prove rule itself lives in :mod:`confirmed`
500	        and is shared with the source-directory export; only the
501	        post-read stability requirement and the import wording are
502	        specific to this entry point.
503	
504	        When ``dir_fd`` and ``name`` are given (whole-directory import),
505	        the pre-open inspection and the post-read re-inspection stay on
506	        the path, but the open itself is ``name`` relative to the pinned
507	        parent directory descriptor: an ancestor directory replaced by a
508	        symbolic link can never redirect the open into the link target.
509	        """
510	        try:
511	            if dir_fd is None:
512	                opened_file = confirmed.confirm_and_open_regular(path)
513	            else:
514	                confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(path)
515	                descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
516	                opened_file = confirmed.ConfirmedOpen(
517	                    descriptor,
518	                    confirmed_status,
519	                    confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status),
520	                )
521	        except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
522	            raise _import_confirmation_error(failure, display) from failure
523	        try:
524	            digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(opened_file.descriptor)
525	        except OSError as error:
526	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
527	        # Import, unlike export, also requires the path itself to still
528	        # name the same unchanged file after the read: an in-place
529	        # rewrite, append, truncation or replacement that landed while
530	        # the bytes were streamed must not register a digest/size pair
531	        # that never coexisted.
532	        try:
533	            after = os.lstat(path)
534	        except OSError as error:
535	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
536	        if not confirmed.same_identity_size_mtime(opened_file.confirmed, after):
537	            raise ValueError(
538	                f"file changed during import: {display} "
539	                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
540	            )
541	        return digest, opened_file.confirmed.st_size
542	
543	    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
544	        self.initialize()
545	        with self._locked():
546	            items = self._read()["items"]
547	        labels = Counter(item["label"] or "unlabeled" for item in items)
548	        return {
549	            "items": len(items),
550	            "bytes": sum(item["size"] for item in items),
551	            "labels": dict(sorted(labels.items())),
552	        }

554	    def find_by_label(self, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
555	        """List samples currently registered under one exact category label.
556	
557	        Matching is exact on the current manifest label: case, surrounding
558	        whitespace and path separators are all kept literally, so ``"cat"``
559	        never matches ``"Cat"`` or ``"cat "``.  The empty string queries
560	        unlabeled samples — records whose stored label is ``None`` or ``""``
561	        — and every matching record's label is reported uniformly as
562	        ``None``.  A genuine class literally named ``"unlabeled"`` is
563	        queried with that text and never mixed with unlabeled samples,
564	        unlike :meth:`summary` which merges them under one display key.
565	
566	        Each record provides the full SHA-256 digest, the source path saved
567	        at first registration, the byte size and the current label;
568	        records are sorted ascending by full digest and ``count`` always
569	        equals the list length.  The query reads the registered records
570	        only — it never opens a source file, and saved split plans' old
571	        labels are neither matched nor rewritten — so a moved, deleted or
572	        unreadable source is still found, and a batch update or undo
573	        committed before the call is immediately reflected.
574	        """
575	        if not isinstance(label, str):
576	            raise BatchError("query label must be a string")
577	        want_unlabeled = label == ""
578	        samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
579	        self.initialize()
580	        with self._locked():
581	            items = self._read()["items"]
582	        for item in items:
583	            stored = item.get("label")
584	            if want_unlabeled:
585	                if not (stored is None or stored == ""):
586	                    continue
587	                current = None
588	            else:
589	                if stored != label:
590	                    continue
591	                current = stored
592	            samples.append(
593	                {
594	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
595	                    "source": item["source"],
596	                    "size": item["size"],
597	                    "label": current,
598	                }
599	            )
600	        samples.sort(key=lambda sample: sample["sha256"])
601	        return {"label": label, "count": len(samples), "samples": samples}

607	    def lookup_label(self, digest: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
608	        """Return ``{"sha256": digest, "label": str | None}`` for a sample.
609	
610	        ``None`` means unlabeled (the manifest may store ``null`` or ``""``).
611	        """
612	        with self._locked():
613	            manifest = self._read()
614	            for item in manifest["items"]:
615	                if item["sha256"] == digest:
616	                    return {"sha256": digest, "label": normalize_label(item.get("label"))}
617	        raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {digest}")

619	    def submit_batch_file(self, path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
620	        """Submit a batch from a UTF-8 JSON file."""
621	        try:
622	            data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
623	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
624	            raise BatchError(f"cannot read batch file: {error}") from error

627	    def submit_batch(self, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
628	        """Validate and apply a batch label update.
629	
630	        The whole batch is verified against the current manifest before any
631	        change is written: missing digests, duplicate records, bad label
632	        types and old-label mismatches reject the batch with no changes.
633	        A successful batch is recorded in history; re-submitting the same
634	        number with the same content returns the original result without
635	        touching anything.
636	        """
637	        number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
638	        with self._locked(create=True):
639	            manifest = self._read()
640	            history = self._read_history()
641	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
642	
643	            for record in records:
644	                if record["sha256"] not in items:
645	                    raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {record['sha256']}")
646	
647	            existing = next(
648	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
649	                None,
650	            )
651	            if existing is not None:
652	                if content_key(existing["records"]) == content_key(records):
653	                    return self._replay_result(existing)
654	                raise BatchError(
655	                    f"batch number {number!r} is already used with different content"
656	                )
657	
658	            for record in records:
659	                current = normalize_label(items[record["sha256"]].get("label"))
660	                if current != record["old"]:
661	                    raise BatchError(
662	                        f"change for {record['sha256']}: expected old label "
663	                        f"{render_label(record['old'])!r} but current label is "
664	                        f"{render_label(current)!r}"
665	                    )
666	
667	            applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
668	            changed_count = 0
669	            for record in records:
670	                item = items[record["sha256"]]
671	                current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
672	                changed = current != record["new"]
673	                revision = self._revision(item)
674	                if changed:
675	                    item["label"] = record["new"]
676	                    revision += 1
677	                    item["rev"] = revision
678	                    changed_count += 1
679	                applied_records.append(
680	                    {**record, "changed": changed, "rev": revision}
681	                )
682	
683	            if changed_count == 0:
684	                # No-op batches occupy no number and write no history.
685	                return {
686	                    "batch": number,
687	                    "status": "no-changes",
688	                    "changed": 0,
689	                    "unchanged": len(records),
690	                    "total": len(records),
691	                }
692	
693	            entry = {
694	                "batch": number,
695	                "records": applied_records,
696	                "changed_count": changed_count,
697	                "undone": False,
698	                "undone_at": None,
699	            }
700	            history["batches"].append(entry)
701	            self._commit(manifest, history)
702	            return {
703	                "batch": number,
704	                "status": "applied",
705	                "changed": changed_count,
706	                "unchanged": len(records) - changed_count,
707	                "total": len(records),
708	            }
709	
710	    def undo_batch(self, number: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
711	        """Undo a successful batch by number.
712	
713	        Only samples the batch actually changed are checked: each must have
714	        the same label revision it had right after the batch (no later
715	        modification, even one that restored the same label).  Repeated
716	        undos are idempotent and do not add history.
717	        """
718	        with self._locked(create=True):
719	            manifest = self._read()
720	            history = self._read_history()
721	            entry = next(
722	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
723	                None,
724	            )
725	            if entry is None:
726	                raise BatchError(f"unknown batch number: {number!r}")
727	            if entry["undone"]:
728	                return {"batch": number, "status": "already-undone", "restored": 0}
729	
730	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
